title: refresh-handshake-interference-in-vpc-peering-causes-apikey-owner-misassignment
creator: Priya Rao
description: Production customer escalations: during VPC peering failover events we observed intermittent apikey owner misassignment in Private deployments. A subset of proxied requests that triggered token refresh paths were briefly bound to the wrong tenant, leading to authorization errors and, in several cases, read access to a different customer's metadata. Issue surfaced after a canary rollout to a subset of VPC-connected private nodes and affected both Dedicated->Private migration customers and one enterprise Private customer with complex peering topology.
impact: Customers experienced intermittent 403/200 mismatches: some requests that should have been denied succeeded against another tenant's resources for up to ~45s during a rolling restart. Several downstream jobs that rely on apikey-owner invariants returned incorrect results. Impact observed across 3 customers; one high-revenue Private customer reported data-access confusion and opened an escalation channel.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure two peered VPCs with edge-proxy in each; enable private deployment and apikey rotation
2) Seed long-lived apikey on tenant A and perform normal traffic routing through proxy node set 1
3) Trigger a rolling restart/failover of proxy node set 1 so traffic shifts to node set 2 while rotation window is active
4) Simultaneously kick off an apikey rotation for the tenant and send a high volume of requests that hit the refresh codepath
5) Observe occasional requests returning a successful 200 for tenant B resources when the request used tenant A's presenting apikey (owner misassignment).
root_cause: Race between the apikey rotation handshake and the VPC peering metadata refresh path. When a proxy loses its cached tenant metadata during peering re-sync there is a small window where the apikey reconciliation path writes owner metadata back using an uninitialized/placeholder peer-id. If a concurrent refresh (token rotation) attaches new owner metadata and the reconcile write is processed out of order, the owner field can be set to the wrong org. TTLs and fastpath cache invalidation were misaligned between the auth service and proxy, and the reconciliation did not use versioned compare-and-set semantics.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix deployed to edge proxies that pauses apikey-owner reconciliation while peer-metadata refresh is in flight; added a short randomized backoff. 2) Temporarily extended apikey metadata TTLs to 120s to reduce reconciliation churn during rollouts. 3) Notified affected customers and disabled canary group while patch validated. 4) Added alerting on anomalous cross-tenant success rates (custom rule).
fix_plan: Short term (this sprint): implement compare-and-set update in auth service for apikey owner writes so out-of-order writes cannot overwrite newer owner metadata
Mid term: introduce a versioned metadata envelope for apikey entries and make proxies perform conditional updates using that version
Long term: add end-to-end integration tests that emulate VPC peering churn + rotation chatter and add a chaos test to CI
Operational: add an audit-mode that logs owner-change events with pre/post owner for 30 days for Private customers
